name: Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them: Overcoming Few-Shot Prompt Order Sensitivity (GlobalE / LocalE probing)
venue: ACL 2022 (Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 8086-8098, Dublin, Ireland); Outstanding Paper Award. First posted on arXiv April 2021 (arXiv:2104.08786).
authors_affiliation: Yao Lu, Max Bartolo, Sebastian Riedel, Pontus Stenetorp (University College London); Alastair Moore (Mishcon de Reya LLP / MDR Research). Lead author: Yao Lu (UCL).
code_url: https://github.com/mdrresearch/mdr-research/tree/main/Fantastically_ordered_prompts (official MDR Research repo hosting paper materials/illustrative code; not a full standalone training repo)
task_domain: QA / NLP text classification under few-shot in-context learning (ICL); demonstration ordering/selection for prompt construction.
problem_setting: Offline, single-model, single-turn in-context learning (no fine-tuning). A small fixed set of n labeled training samples (typically 4-shot; 1-shot for DBPedia, 2-shot for AGNews due to GPT-2 1024-token context limit) is given. The paper studies sensitivity of few-shot ICL accuracy to the ORDER (permutation) of these demonstrations and proposes a true-few-shot method (no held-out labeled dev set, following Perez et al. 2021) to pick performant orderings. Supervision beyond the few training samples is unavailable; an artificial unlabeled 'probing set' is self-generated by the LM. No interaction with an environment; no multi-agent setting.
what_is_retrieved: Demonstration permutations (orderings of the same fixed set of few-shot demos). The method selects/ranks candidate orderings rather than retrieving demos from a corpus; it also self-generates an artificial probing set used for scoring orderings.
retrieval_grounding: Neither a static external corpus nor a growing episodic memory in the classic RAG sense: the 'candidate pool' is the n! permutations of one fixed small training set, and the scoring data (probing set) is generated on the fly by the LM itself. Best characterized as self-generated / internal grounding (LM as data source), not external-corpus retrieval.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k selection over candidate orderings: from the up-to-24 (n!) candidate permutations, rank by entropy probing metric and keep the top k (k=4 used; K=1 also works). Objective is selecting a small set of performant orderings, not completeness recovery.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is positioned as prompt-order selection for ICL.
retrieval_unit: A full prompt = an ordered concatenation (permutation) of the few-shot demonstrations (single demos linearized via a template and concatenated). The selectable unit is a demonstration ordering/permutation, not an individual document or trajectory.
index_source: Test-time-induced and ephemeral: candidate orderings are enumerated from one fixed training set, and the artificial probing set used to score them is generated online by sampling from the LM (temperature t=2, max generation length 128, with block n-gram repetition to encourage diverse generation). No persistent offline index.
index_structure_topology: Flat enumeration of permutations (up to 24 = 4! candidate orderings); no vector index, graph, or hierarchy. The probing set is a flat collection of LM-generated, label-discarded sentences.
retriever_type: Not a conventional retriever. Selection is done by an LM-as-scorer / generative-probing mechanism: the same LM generates a probing set and produces predicted-label distributions, then candidates are ranked by an entropy statistic (GlobalE / LocalE). No BM25/dense embedding retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (no trained retriever). Selection uses an unsupervised, training-free statistic over self-generated probes: GlobalE (entropy of the predicted category-label distribution over the probing set) and LocalE (mean per-example prediction entropy). Higher entropy is preferred (avoids degenerate, highly unbalanced or over-confident predictions). No similarity contrastive learning, no RL.
query_construction: Each candidate prompt c_m is the concatenation of one permutation of the linearized training samples (template T(x,y) = 'input: x ... label: y'). To build the probing set, each candidate prompt is itself used as context to sample a continuation g_m ~ P(.|c_m; theta); the generated probes (T^{-1}(g_m), labels discarded) form the unlabeled dev set against which all candidates are scored.
query_granularity: Task-level / one-shot: ordering selection happens once at prompt-construction time (t=0) for the fixed demo set; not per-step or per-test-instance.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: the performant orderings are selected once before inference, then reused for all test examples of the task.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (no dynamic trigger): probing-set generation and entropy ranking are performed once during prompt construction; not confidence/uncertainty/agent-triggered.
reranking: Yes - the core mechanism is a (re)ranking of candidate orderings by an entropy probing metric (GlobalE or LocalE), then selecting the top-k (k=4). It is an entropy-statistic ranker, not a cross-encoder; no RRF.
retrieved_context_refinement: Selection/ranking only. Probes generated by the LM have their predicted labels discarded (kept as unlabeled inputs because label validity is not guaranteed); candidate orderings are then ranked and truncated to top-k. No document distillation or compression of the demos themselves.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the selected performant ordering(s) of the few-shot demonstrations are placed in the LM context as the in-context-learning prompt; no training signal, no skill reuse, no latent injection.
planning_integration: One-shot exemplars at prompt/inference time. Selected orderings serve directly as the few-shot context; there is no planner, no tree search, no per-step retrieval.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: a single classification prediction is produced from the fixed selected prompt; no interleaving of retrieval with multi-step reasoning.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; selected demos are used verbatim as ICL exemplars).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw few-shot demonstrations (template-linearized sentence+label pairs) injected verbatim in a chosen order; surface form is plain natural-language exemplars.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw single demonstrations (ordered set thereof); no distilled strategy, skill, or workflow abstraction.
noise_robustness_mechanism: The entropy-based selection itself acts as a guard against degenerate prompts: GlobalE penalizes orderings that yield highly unbalanced predicted-label distributions and LocalE penalizes overconfident/poorly-calibrated predictions, thereby filtering 'bad' orderings. No retriever-aware training or self-reflection module.
memory_type: none (no persistent memory; the probing set is transient and discarded after selection).
write_back: False - nothing is written back to a persistent store; the artificial probing set is generated, used for ranking, and not retained as reusable memory.
online_growth: False - no store grows during deployment; the candidate pool is fixed (permutations of one training set) and probes are regenerated per selection, not accumulated.
write_back_trigger: never - no write-back of experiences/cases/skills occurs.
failure_experience_usage: N/A - no explicit storage of failed experiences. (Indirectly, degenerate/non-performant orderings are identified and discarded via low/abnormal entropy, but they are not stored.)
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No - selection is a fixed unsupervised entropy statistic over self-generated probes, not a learned/RL-optimized policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No - single-model, no shared memory across agents. Notably, the paper shows performant orderings are NOT transferable across model sizes (e.g., Spearman correlation 0.05 between GPT-3 2.7B and 175B), arguing against cross-model sharing.
benchmarks: Eleven text-classification tasks: SST-2, SST-5, MR, CR, MPQA, Subj, TREC, AGNews, DBPedia, CB, RTE. Models: GPT-2 (0.1B/base, 0.3B/medium, 0.8B/large, 1.5B/XL) and GPT-3 (2.7B and 175B via OpenAI API).
benchmark_family: QA / text classification (sentiment: SST-2, SST-5, MR, CR, MPQA; subjectivity: Subj; question type: TREC; topic: AGNews, DBPedia; NLI: CB, RTE). Not a planning/agentic/embodied/tool benchmark family.
baselines: Baseline = mean accuracy over all candidate prompt orderings (no probing/selection); Majority baseline (always predict majority label, lower bound); Oracle (top-4 orderings selected using the true validation set, upper bound); Split Training Set (split the 4-shot training samples into train/dev and select orderings by dev-set performance); calibration along the lines of Zhao et al. 2021 (contextual calibration) discussed in analysis. Compared GlobalE vs LocalE against these.
key_metrics: Classification accuracy (mean and standard deviation across orderings/sample sets); relative improvement over the no-selection baseline; Spearman's rank correlation (for the transferability analysis of orderings across models).
headline_result: GlobalE yields on average a 13% relative improvement in accuracy over the no-probing baseline across the eleven text-classification tasks and across all model sizes (GPT-2 0.1B to GPT-3 175B); LocalE gives ~9.6% average relative improvement. Variance across orderings is also substantially reduced; up to ~30% relative improvement on high-variance tasks/models, and +4.9% for GPT-3 175B on CB.
ablations: GlobalE vs LocalE comparison (GlobalE > LocalE: 13% vs 9.6% avg relative gain). Top-K selection sweep (Figure 8): K from 1..24, K=24 equals the all-orderings baseline; negative-sloped curves confirm entropy ranks performant orderings well; K=4 chosen for stability though K=1 often works. Robustness across 4 different prompt templates on SST-2 (Tables 3-4): selection helps across templates. Comparison to 'Split Training Set' (Table 5): both GlobalE and LocalE beat splitting the few-shot set into train/dev across all GPT-2 sizes, supporting the true-few-shot claim. Analysis ablations: order sensitivity persists across model sizes, varying number of shots, sample subsets, and label patterns; good orderings are non-transferable across models (low pairwise Spearman, e.g., 0.05 between 2.7B and 175B); calibration (Zhao et al. 2021) raises mean accuracy but leaves variance high.
evaluation_decoupling: No separate intrinsic retrieval metric (no Recall@k/nDCG). The entropy probing score (GlobalE/LocalE) is the internal ranking signal; effectiveness is validated end-to-end via downstream classification accuracy of selected orderings (and via Top-K-vs-accuracy curves), not via a decoupled retrieval-quality metric.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final classification accuracy and its variance). Process-level analysis is qualitative/diagnostic (predicted-label distribution balance, calibration, Spearman correlations of orderings) rather than a scored intermediate-process metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Cost is from generating the probing set: for each of up to 24 candidate orderings, sample one continuation (max 128 tokens, temperature 2, block n-gram repetition) and then run predictions over the probing set to compute entropy. This requires only the few-shot training samples and the LM (no extra labeled data / no held-out dev set). The paper frames selection as a 'safe operation' (marginal gain at worst, large gains on high-variance settings) but does not report wall-clock latency or API-dollar cost figures explicitly. [uncertain] exact compute/latency numbers.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k selection: k=4 performant orderings kept (out of up to 24). Prompt size constrained by GPT-2's 1024 word-piece context window, hence 4-shot generally, 2-shot for AGNews, 1-shot for DBPedia; probing-set generation capped at 128 tokens. Not budget-adaptive beyond these fixed shot counts.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper). For context, evaluation uses subsets of standard validation sets across 11 established classification datasets; an LM-generated artificial 'probing set' is constructed at test time (examples shown in Table 9), with predicted labels discarded.
builds_on: GPT-3 / in-context learning (Brown et al. 2020); GPT-2 (Radford et al. 2019); true-few-shot evaluation without a held-out dev set (Perez et al. 2021); contextual calibration (Zhao et al. 2021); prompt/template design work (Shin et al. 2020 AutoPrompt; Gao et al. 2020 LM-BFF; Jiang et al. 2020; Schick & Schutze 2020).
contrasts_with: Liu et al. 2021 (KATE: kNN demo retrieval over a standard-size training set, which concluded ordering has little effect after relevance retrieval) - this paper, using only a few-shot set without a large pool, reaches the opposite conclusion that order matters greatly. Also contrasts with using a held-out/split validation set for ordering selection (shown inferior to entropy probing) and with template-quality-focused prompt-design work that ignored ordering. Contrasts fine-tuning (order-insensitive, <1% std per Gao et al. 2020) with ICL (highly order-sensitive).
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval/selection): a foundational ordering-sensitivity work. It establishes few-shot prompt-order sensitivity and introduces an entropy-statistic probing method over an LM-generated artificial dev set to select performant permutations - a precursor/sibling to demonstration-selection and ordering-optimization methods (e.g., later many-shot order-optimization work that critiques GlobalE/LocalE as heuristic).
